title: Legacy Embed Client Gateway: Error Normalization and Pagination Bridge
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Provide a lightweight compatibility gateway that sits in front of the canonical embeddings/rerank endpoints to: (1) translate legacy client pagination (Link header / page tokens / offset semantics) into the new cursor-based cursor_id+cursor_pos contract; (2) normalize and extend HTTP error responses into a stable Redwood error taxonomy for downstream SDKs and retry logic; and (3) emit telemetry to validate parity and drive client migrations. This work reduces breakage for customers who cannot migrate immediately and enables staged deprecation of legacy pagination semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway correctly translates Link header and page/offset query parameters to cursor token responses (idempotent, deterministic mapping) for at least 95% of fixture corpus

Errors returned by the gateway conform to the Redwood canonical error shape: {code, type, message, retryable, hints} and map legacy HTTP codes to appropriate types (4xx client, 5xx server, 429 rate, 503 capacity).
SDK integration tests (JS and Python) pass against the gateway with no code changes for existing legacy clients using offset/paginated endpoints.
Performance overhead: median added latency <= 8ms, p99 <= 25ms on production-like load for the gateway translation path.
Telemetry dashboards created: parity-success-rate, normalized-error-rate, client-version-usage, migration-progress-by-customer.
Migration playbook (customer-facing) and deprecation schedule published to docs and linked in changelog.
design_notes: Proxy will be implemented as an API gateway layer with a small translation module; not a full-blown protocol adapter to avoid coupling with serving runtime.
Pagination mapping must be reversible so that logs and audit traces can tie legacy client requests to canonical cursor values for debugging and replay.
Error taxonomy: introduce 'retryable' boolean and 'hints' array to surface idempotency or backoff guidance. Keep original HTTP status for observability but key clients on canonical 'code' field.
Streaming and structured output: gateway should pass through streaming token frames for embed/rerank streaming calls and only apply pagination mapping to non-streamed list responses.
Quota and rate-limit semantics maintained; gateway will forward X-RateLimit and include mapped headers where necessary.
Gateway config will support per-tenant rules to enable feature-flagged translation and phased rollouts.
work_breakdown: PM: finalize acceptance criteria and customer communication plan
Design: API contract spec for gateway translation and canonical error model (owner: DES/UX)
Engineering: build translation module, unit + integration tests, add telemetry hooks
SDK: add compatibility harness in CI that runs legacy client fixtures against gateway
Docs: migration guide, changelog entry, sample curl snippets for legacy clients
SRE: performance testing and capacity plan for gateway layer
Security: threat model review and RBAC for per-tenant config UI
risks: Semantic mismatches: some legacy clients rely on subtle ordering/offset assumptions that cannot be deterministically mapped to cursors — will require per-customer exceptions.
Latency overhead: extra network hop could push tight-latency customers past SLOs; mitigation is co-locating gateway in same service mesh and optimizing hot path.
Operational complexity: managing per-tenant migration flags increases operational surface area and could cause drift if not monitored.
Auditability: translation must preserve enough context to debug billing/requests — need deterministic tokenization and stable hash scheme.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (Pilot): enable gateway for 5 low-risk customers and run compatibility tests for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (Canary): widen to 20 customers with mixed load profiles; monitor parity-success-rate and error drift.
Phase 3 (Open): automatic opt-in for legacy client UA strings; update docs and start 60-day migration notices for non-upgraded clients.
Phase 4 (Deprecation): after 6 months, begin rejecting legacy pagination if customers have not migrated (with clear error messages and deprecation code).
rollout_criteria: Parity-success-rate >= 99% during canary for non-edge fixtures
No unhandled customer-facing 5xx spikes attributable to translation layer for 72h
Telemetry coverage validated: 90% of legacy requests have cursor mapping traces
Docs and support playbook published and reviewed by CS and Legal
tests: Compatibility fixture set covering: Link header pages, offset-based requests, empty result sets, large-page edge cases, and concurrent paginated reads
Chaos test: simulate intermittent 500s from origin service and verify gateway surface normalizable errors and backoff hints
Latency test: 95th and 99th percentile under expected throughput load
SDK regression tests: run against gateway without code changes; assert no behavior differences in response shape for supported clients
